headline: South Asia: 'Grave provocation': Pakistan condemns Houthi attack on power facility in Madina
script:
Good afternoon. This is your global conflict briefing.

BOTTOM LINE UP FRONT:
- South Asia: 'Grave provocation': Pakistan condemns Houthi attack on power facility in Madina.
- Western Russia: Zelenskyy on Russian strikes on Kyiv: They want Ukrainians to leave the capital.
- Asia: Ethiopia and Eritrea sever diplomatic ties as northern fighting escalates.

Full breakdown follows.

NORTH AMERICA
United States - bottom line: US Navy awards RTX’s Raytheon $24.4B for SM-6 missiles amid stockpile concerns.
- Military Times, 19 hours ago: US Navy awards RTX’s Raytheon $24.4B for SM-6 missiles amid stockpile concerns.
The deal for the SM-6 interceptors comes as the Pentagon pushes to replenish munitions stockpiles depleted by conflicts in the Middle East.
- Military Times, one day ago: Navy Expeditionary Combat Command rebranded to reflect warfare evolution.
CNO Adm. Daryl Caudle announced that the Navy Expeditionary Combat Command will now be known as Commander, Navy Expeditionary Forces.
- Military Times, 4 hours ago: Marine Corps plans new warfighter test for future generals.
Following Pentagon guidelines, the Marine Corps is developing and testing its own Joint Warfighter Evaluation.
- Military Times, 23 hours ago: Boeing adds to big week with first full-rate Grey Wolf helicopter order.
The U.S. Air Force awarded Boeing a roughly $85 million contract for four more MH-139A Grey Wolf helicopters, with the first under full-rate production.
The Caribbean - bottom line: Doctors demand timeline for IDT ruling.
- Jamaica Gleaner, 12 hours ago: Doctors demand timeline for IDT ruling.
The Jamaica Medical Doctors Association (JMDA) is calling for the Industrial Disputes Tribunal (IDT) to provide a timeline for delivering its ruling in the longstanding dispute between doctors and the Ministry of Health and Wellness over overtime payments. In a press release, JMDA President Jubilee Brown-Service said it took note of the IDT’s September 30 statement, which conceded that “justice delayed is justice denied”. “We call on the IDT to stop denying justice to our doctors by handing down its award without further delay,” the JMDA declared.
Central America: no notable developments in the last 48 hours.

SOUTH AMERICA
South America - bottom line: Argentine rugby player murdered in Paris honored by French league.
- Buenos Aires Herald, 23 hours ago: Argentine rugby player murdered in Paris honored by French league.
Federico Aramburú, who was killed in March 2022 after a bar brawl, will lend his name to a social commitment award La entrada Argentine rugby player murdered in Paris honored by French league se publicó primero en Buenos Aires Herald.

EUROPE
Western Russia - bottom line: Zelenskyy on Russian strikes on Kyiv: They want Ukrainians to leave the capital.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Zelenskyy on Russian strikes on Kyiv: They want Ukrainians to leave the capital.
Zelenskyy says Russia is intensifying attacks on civilian targets to force Ukrainians to leave Kyiv and predicts further escalation ahead of the US midterm elections.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 5 hours ago: Russians strike Mykolaiv: 3 injured, warehouses, offices and hotel damaged.
Three people were injured and port infrastructure, an administrative building, warehouses, offices and a hotel and restaurant site were damaged in Russian strikes on Mykolaiv on 2 October.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 3 hours ago: "Anarchist, feminist, vegan": combat medic and activist Ivanna Kutsenko killed in action.
Ivanna "Haika" Kutsenko, a 33-year-old marine and feminist activist, has been killed by Russian artillery fire.
- Ukrainska Pravda, 6 hours ago: Russians attack petrol station in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast twice.
Russian forces have twice attacked a petrol station belonging to Ukrnafta, Ukraine's largest oil producer, in Dnipropetrovsk Oblast, with no casualties reported.
Southern Europe - bottom line: Biljana Plavsic, Bosnian Serb War Criminal Who Withdrew Her Remorse.
- Balkan Insight, 2 hours ago: Biljana Plavsic, Bosnian Serb War Criminal Who Withdrew Her Remorse.
Plavsic, who died this week, was the only high-ranking woman political leader prosecuted for mass atrocities by the Yugoslav war crimes tribunal. She expressed sorrow for these acts in court – but then changed her mind.
- Balkan Insight, 2 hours ago: Week in Review: Elections and Struggles.
Women get a raw deal at elections in Bosnia, a spy chief’s arrest raises security questions in Albania and protesters challenge war crimes verdicts in Kosovo - plus much more in our selection of this week’s Balkan Insight Premium stories.
- Politico Europe, 7 hours ago: Tories warn Burnham’s EU ‘pandering’ will shred post-Brexit trade deals.
Three former ministers tell POLITICO of “grave consequences” if the U.K. moves closer to the EU under prime minister's bid for a revamped relationship.
- Balkan Insight, 11 hours ago: By Skoda and By Bike: Serbia’s Not Completely Even Election Race.
Crowdfunding, donations and the volunteer spirit are driving Serbia’s cycling students towards the election finish line on October 25 - while Aleksandar Vucic is promoting a ‘man of the people’ image as he tours the country by car.

AFRICA
Africa - bottom line: Ethiopia: Who Gets to Author Ethiopia's Political Order? Why the Crisis Is About More Than Identity Politics.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 3 hours ago: Ethiopia: Who Gets to Author Ethiopia's Political Order? Why the Crisis Is About More Than Identity Politics.
[Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- A familiar explanation of Ethiopia's recurring crises starts with identity: politics organized around nationality can harden boundaries, reward exclusionary mobilization, and expose minorities, migrants, mixed communities, and dissenters to exclusion when democratic protections are weak. International Crisis Group and other scholars have long raised these concerns.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 7 hours ago: Nigeria: Troops Rescue 10 Prospective Corps Members Abducted in Imo.
[Vanguard] Troops of the Nigerian Army have neutralised 16 terrorists and recovered weapons after repelling simultaneous attacks in Adamawa.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, 8 hours ago: Uganda: Uganda to Host Inaugural Conference On Military Operations Other Than War.
[Nile Post] Uganda will next week host the inaugural Conference on Military Operations Other Than War (MOOTW), bringing together military commanders, regional security bodies and peace support mission leaders from across Africa to discuss emerging security threats and non-traditional approaches to conflict management.
- AllAfrica - Conflict, one hour ago: Ethiopia: Alamata Fighting Leaves Trail of Civilian Casualties - Adigrat Eparch Appeals for Help.
[Addis Standard] Addis Abeba -- More than 50 civilians have reportedly been killed in and around Alamata, southern Tigray, during several days of intense fighting in late September, as renewed hostilities in northern Ethiopia leave residents displaced, medical facilities overwhelmed and humanitarian access increasingly difficult.

South Africa - bottom line: South Africa: Zero-Tolerance Towards Fraud Affirmed.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, just now: South Africa: Zero-Tolerance Towards Fraud Affirmed.
[SAnews.gov.za] The Border Management Authority (BMA) has reaffirmed its zero-tolerance approach to fraud, corruption and misconduct at South Africa's borders and ports of entry.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 9 hours ago: South Africa: Would Homegrown LEN Cost More? Why SA Should Still Make the HIV Prevention Jab.
[Bhekisisa] South Africa wants to make the six-monthly HIV prevention injection lenacapavir locally. But cheaper generics made elsewhere are expected from 2027. Vinodh Aroon Edward explains why getting the jab to people quickly must come first -- while South Africa builds the skills to make it here.
- AllAfrica - Southern Africa, 12 hours ago: Zimbabwe: Chivayo, Wife, Three Others' Heavily Dismembered Bodies Removed From Crash Site After 18-Hour Operation.
[New Zimbabwe] THE heavily dismembered bodies of controversial businessman Wicknell Chivayo, his wife Lucy Muteke and three others killed in a plane crash were finally removed from the wreckage site about 18 hours after the tragedy.

ASIA
South Asia - bottom line: 'Grave provocation': Pakistan condemns Houthi attack on power facility in Madina.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 11 hours ago: 'Grave provocation': Pakistan condemns Houthi attack on power facility in Madina.
Pakistan on Friday strongly condemned an attack by the Houthi militia on the Taibah power distribution station in Madina on Sept 29, describing it as a “grave provocation” and a threat to regional peace and security. In a statement, the Foreign Office (FO) said the attack targeted civilian infrastructure supplying electricity to the Holy Prophet’s (PBUH) Mosque. “The sanctity of the Two Holy Mosques and the safety of worshippers and pilgrims must be respected under all circumstances,” the FO said.
- Dawn (Pakistan), one hour ago: Army's top brass warns of 'decisive force' against any 'May 9-like situation'.
The army’s top brass on Friday warned that any attempt at creating agitation or a “May 9-like situation” would be dealt with “decisive force”, according to the military’s media wing. The warning came during the 277th Corps Commanders’ Conference in Rawalpindi, which was presided over by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 2 hours ago: Dar says Makkah defence pact committee to meet next week on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia.
Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar said on Friday that a meeting of Makkah Defence Alliance’s Strategic Political Defence Committee (SPDC) would take place in Riyadh next week, adding that it would focus on Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia. He made the remarks while addressing a press briefing detailing the Pakistan delegation’s engagements at the 81st session of the United Nations General Assembly (UNGA) in New York in September, as well as high-level meetings that took place on its sidelines.
- Dawn (Pakistan), 10 hours ago: 7 terrorists eliminated in KP’s North Waziristan IBO: state media.
Seven terrorists were killed in the Eidak area of Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s North Waziristan district during an intelligence-based operation (IBO), state media reported on Friday, citing security sources. “Security forces pursued the terrorists of Fitna al Khawarij with determination and combat skills and destroyed their hideouts,” Radio Pakistan said. Fitna al Khawarij is a term the state uses for terrorists belonging to the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP). President Asif Ali Zardari lauded security forces for the successful operation, a statement issued by his office said.

Ethiopia and Eritrea broke diplomatic ties on Thursday, accusing each other of stoking internal conflicts as fighting continued in northern Ethiopia. Ethiopia accuses Eritrea of backing a rebel group, the Tigray People’s Liberation Front (TPLF), which launched a major assault against government forces last week, raising fears of a return to the devastating 2020–2022 civil war that killed an estimated 600,000 people. The Japanese government on Friday announced additional sanctions against Russia amid the ongoing invasion of Ukraine, targeting a so-called shadow fleet of vessels engaged in transporting sanctioned oil from Russia. Joining international efforts to crack down on sanctions evasion by the fleet, Japan has decided to impose restrictions on the provision of services to 35 vessels, according to the Foreign Ministry. China has set up several new institutions at military academies to train specialists in hi-tech and discipline inspection as the People’s Liberation Army (PLA) works towards its centennial modernisation goals. The College of Unmanned and Intelligent Engineering, the College of Combat Support NCOs (Non-Commissioned Officers) and the College of Equipment Support NCOs were established within the PLA Army Engineering University on Wednesday.
